precepts.text: Unto us a child is born, and the government shall be upon his shoulder; the church of Acts 7 is the government of Christ. He is called the everlasting Father because much of the Old Testament's Father is Christ; have I been so long time with you, Philip, and hast thou not known me? Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end: it starts as a mustard seed and grows, and once started there is no stopping it.
precepts.point: Be preemptive with the Christians who run to Exodus 12:38, the mixed multitude, to say other nations were part of the church. Leviticus 25:45-46: of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you shall ye buy, and they shall be your bondmen for ever. The mixed multitude were our slaves.

note.label: America: Hammer of the Earth

precepts.why:
“For unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given: and the government shall be upon his shoulder.” When Acts 7:38 speaks of “the church in the wilderness”, it is speaking of the government of Christ. That church was Israel, the twelve tribes, and it is his government that rests upon his shoulder.

“And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” Christ is called the everlasting Father because many times in the Old Testament, when you read about the Father, it is making reference to Christ. That is why, when Philip asked Christ to show them the Father, Christ answered that he had been so long time with him and still Philip had not known him. Christ is letting you know: I am the father that created you. Not the Father, but your father.

“Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” Increase means it starts small. Christ said the kingdom of heaven starts like a mustard seed, but in the end it is the largest. Once that mustard seed is planted and growing, there is no stopping it. It sits “upon the throne of David, and upon his kingdom, to order it, and to establish it with judgment and with justice from henceforth even for ever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will perform this.”

This truth cannot be stopped. No matter how many Israelites they attempt to kill or arrest, the church that was in the wilderness, the government on Christ’s shoulder, keeps increasing and has no end.

precepts.text: In the days of these kings, the ten toes of iron and clay, America, shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom which shall never be destroyed. Israelites are waking up all over the world now. Asked in an interview how we differ from the Panthers, Martin Luther King, SNCC, or the Young Lords: those were man-made and had an end, most no longer exist, but this kingdom shall never be destroyed.
precepts.point: Be preemptive with the Christians who run to Exodus 12:38, the mixed multitude, to say other nations were part of the church. Leviticus 25:45-46: of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you shall ye buy, and they shall be your bondmen for ever. The mixed multitude were our slaves.

note.label: America: Hammer of the Earth

precepts.why:
“And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed.” These kings are the last kings of the image, the ten toes, the ten common markets, and America is that iron and that clay. In their days God sets up his kingdom, and that is what is happening now: Israelites are waking up all over the world.

“Which shall never be destroyed.” That says the same thing as Isaiah 9: “Of the increase of his government and peace there shall be no end.” The church in the wilderness, the twelve tribes under Christ’s government, is a kingdom God himself sets up, and it will not be brought down.

That is the difference between this truth and the movements of men. Asked in an interview how Israel in Christ differs from the Black Panthers, Martin Luther King, SNCC or the Young Lords, the answer was plain: those were all man-made, they all had an end, and most of them do not even exist today. This kingdom is not man-made.

“And the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.” The God of heaven set it up, so no government of this world can stop it.

precepts.text: Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God; upon this rock, Christ himself, I will build my church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it. They murdered Nat Turner, Denmark Vesey, and Gabriel Prosser, men who knew they were Israelites, and through whispers and hushes the word kept going. Get the proper understanding of the word and it cannot be stopped.
precepts.point: Be preemptive with the Christians who run to Exodus 12:38, the mixed multitude, to say other nations were part of the church. Leviticus 25:45-46: of the children of the strangers that sojourn among you shall ye buy, and they shall be your bondmen for ever. The mixed multitude were our slaves.

note.label: America: Hammer of the Earth

precepts.why:
Christ asks, “But whom say ye that I am?” and Peter answers, “Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.” Christ tells him “flesh and blood hath not revealed it unto thee, but my Father which is in heaven.”

Then verse 18 is the key: “upon this rock I will build my church”. That rock is Christ himself, not Peter. And the church he builds is the same government we read of in Isaiah 9, the same church in the wilderness in Acts 7:38: Israel.

“And the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.” There is no stopping us. Once you get the proper understanding of the word of God, you cannot stop it; it is going to flourish and grow. The gates of hell will attempt to stop it, but they will not prevail. They attempted it when they murdered Nat Turner, Denmark Vesey and Gabriel Prosser, men who knew they were Israelites. They said kill them, and it did not stop. Through whispers and hushes, this word kept going.

The gates of hell are not a flesh and blood enemy: “For we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places.” In our carnal mind we think that if we organize we can overthrow the system, but we cannot. The governments of this earth are set up by Satan, and God allows it. Only God can bring all that down, and Christ has promised that none of it will prevail against his church.

precepts.text: Ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves. It is idolatry. God never gave us that star; Solomon picked it up dabbling in witchcraft.
precepts.point: Ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them. Moloch is Baal, both the devil, and the star is the hexagram, which cannot be found anywhere in the Bible as God's sign.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
The Iranians burned large statues of a horned, bull-headed figure bearing the so-called Star of David, and they knew what they were doing: they were burning statues of Baal. That is not the Star of David. You cannot find it anywhere in the Bible; it is a sign in the occult.

Stephen said, “Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.” If you didn't know, Moloch is Baal: the same thing, both the devil. The star is the star of their god, the devil, Baal or Moloch.

Stephen was quoting Amos: “But ye have borne the tabernacle of your Moloch and Chiun your images, the star of your god, which ye made to yourselves.” Which ye made to yourselves: it is idolatry. God did not give us that star. When King Solomon was dabbling in witchcraft, that is how he got that star; God never gave it to us.

So the star so-called Israel and America carry is the star of Baal, and Baal worship shows up in plain sight: the bull's head statue at the 1933 Chicago World's Fair on Jewish Day, the giant mechanical bull at the 2022 Commonwealth Games, the bull on Wall Street. Even bullheaded, stupidly stubborn, comes from Baal worship, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. That idolatry is why Israel was carried away, and why we are in captivity today.

precepts.text: Stephen told the council, As your fathers did, so do ye; which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? They were cut to the heart because they knew exactly which grandfathers killed which prophets.
precepts.point: They have thrown down thine altars and slain thy prophets, and I, even I only, am left. Israel's rulers killed the prophets who taught against them. The same people mock the purple and gold today.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: the Grafted in Strangers

precepts.why:
Stephen prophesied against the rulers, the builders of his time: “Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.” As your fathers did, so do you.

“Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? and they have slain them which shewed before of the coming of the Just One”. The prophets were killed in the Old Testament, and who were they prophesying of? The Just One. So when the prophets prophesied of a Messiah, they were killed. The killers who got away with it had children, and their children knew who they had killed. Then when Christ was born, they killed him too: “of whom ye have been now the betrayers and murderers: Who have received the law by the disposition of angels, and have not kept it.”

“When they heard these things, they were cut to the heart, and they gnashed on him with their teeth.” Why cut to the heart? Because they knew. Stephen was in the spirit; he saw their fathers killing the prophets: your father killed Zechariah, your father killed Isaiah. They knew and did not care, and they were pissed off that he said it. They gnashed on him, cursing him out.

The prophets were sent to bring us back to God, and the rulers hated them because the prophets could see right through them. It was the same spirit in Elijah’s day, in Christ’s day, and in Rome against the apostles, and it is the same spirit today.

precepts.text: The church in the wilderness was the twelve tribes, not the Baptists, Pentecostals and Catholics your enemies made up.
precepts.point: I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. That is the church fathers, not Churchill or Martin Luther.

precepts.text: His seed should sojourn in a strange land, in bondage, and be evil entreated four hundred years.
precepts.point: Abram himself would go to his fathers in peace and be buried in a good old age; and the seed would return in the fourth generation, for the iniquity of the Amorites was not yet full.

note.label: Genesis 15: The Covenant and the Four Hundred Years

precepts.why:
Stephen repeats the prophecy: “God spake on this wise, That his seed should sojourn in a strange land; and that they should bring them into bondage, and entreat them evil four hundred years.” Same words as Genesis 15:13: a stranger in a land that is not theirs, serving them, afflicted four hundred years.

This was fulfilled in Egypt. Abram was told to “know of a surety” that it would happen to his seed, and Stephen, looking back, shows it did.

precepts.text: There came a dearth over all the land of Egypt and Chanaan, and our fathers found no sustenance; dearth is famine.
precepts.point: The dearth was in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread, because Joseph had stored up the seven years of plenty. All countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn.

note.label: Genesis 41: Pharaoh's Dreams and Joseph's Rise Over Egypt

precepts.why:
“Now there came a dearth over all the land of Egypt and Chanaan, and great affliction: and our fathers found no sustenance.” Another word for dearth is famine: no food, no sustenance to nourish the body. That is what the seven years of dearth were, “according as Joseph had said”, and it reached Chanaan where the fathers were, so that they found no sustenance.

But “in all the land of Egypt there was bread”, because Joseph had stored up the seven years of plenty. So Pharaoh sent all the Egyptians to Joseph, and all countries came into Egypt to Joseph for to buy corn, for the famine was so sore in all lands.

precepts.text: The patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt; but God was with him, delivered him out of all his afflictions, and made him governor.
precepts.point: The famine itself was called by the Most High, and the man was sent before them, even Joseph, sold for a servant, whose feet they hurt with fetters. The fetters and the iron are the prison where the king's prisoners were bound.

note.label: Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren

precepts.why:
“And the patriarchs, moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt: but God was with him, And delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favour and wisdom in the sight of Pharaoh king of Egypt; and he made him governor over Egypt and all his house.” Envy sold him; God was with him.

That is what Joseph told his brethren: “it was not you that sent me hither, but God: and he hath made me a father to Pharaoh, and lord of all his house, and a ruler throughout all the land of Egypt.” The Most High sent him before them to preserve life and to save the whole house of Israel by a great deliverance. Had he not been in Egypt, they would have died in the famine.

precepts.text: There came a dearth over all the land, and when Jacob heard that there was corn in Egypt, he sent out our fathers; Joseph's saving carried the family.
precepts.point: Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers. Applying these attributes makes better men, women, brothers, and sisters, to bring forth the nation unto the kingdom of God.

note.label: Genesis 45: Joseph Made Known unto His Brethren

precepts.why:
“Now there came a dearth over all the land of Egypt and Chanaan, and great affliction: and our fathers found no sustenance. But when Jacob heard that there was corn in Egypt, he sent out our fathers first.” Jacob knew there was corn in Egypt because Joseph had already told Pharaoh exactly what to do to save up in the time of tribulation; when Jacob heard, he sent out the fathers.

“And at the second time Joseph was made known to his brethren; and Joseph’s kindred was made known unto Pharaoh. Then sent Joseph, and called his father Jacob to him, and all his kindred, threescore and fifteen souls.” That is where the brethren are here, come back up to Canaan with the words of Joseph and the wagons: Joseph’s saving carried the whole family, and Israel said, “I will go and see him before I die.”

precepts.text: In which time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father's house three months.
precepts.point: The woman conceived and bare a son, and when she saw him that he was a goodly child, she hid him three months. Goodly means the child was exceeding fair; there was something special about this child from his birth.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

precepts.why:
The woman “saw him that he was a goodly child”. Stephen tells what goodly means: “In which time Moses was born, and was exceeding fair, and nourished up in his father’s house three months”.

Goodly is exceeding fair. And the three months Exodus gives, “she hid him three months”, are the three months he was nourished up in his father’s house. There was something special about this child from his birth.

precepts.text: There appeared to Moses in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush; him did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.
precepts.point: The same angel went before Israel out of Egypt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee; beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not, for my name is in him.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
Stephen recounts the bush. “And when forty years were expired, there appeared to him in the wilderness of mount Sina an angel of the Lord in a flame of fire in a bush.” Moses drew near, “the voice of the Lord came unto him, Saying, I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob”, and “Put off thy shoes from thy feet: for the place where thou standest is holy ground.” It is the same account as Exodus 3, the angel in the flame and the voice of the Lord out of the bush.

Then Stephen tells who that angel was to Moses: “This Moses whom they refused, saying, Who made thee a ruler and a judge? the same did God send to be a ruler and a deliverer by the hand of the angel which appeared to him in the bush.” The angel which appeared in the bush is the one who sent Moses to deliver Israel and brought them out “after that he had shewed wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red sea, and in the wilderness forty years.”

Precept upon precept with Joshua 5 and Hebrews 2, this identifies the angel of the Lord in the burning bush: it was Christ.

precepts.text: This is that Moses which said, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; he was in the church in the wilderness with the angel which spake to him in the mount Sina.
precepts.point: The same angel went before Israel out of Egypt: Behold, I send an Angel before thee; beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not, for my name is in him.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

precepts.why:
“This is that Moses, which said unto the children of Israel, A prophet shall the Lord your God raise up unto you of your brethren, like unto me; him shall ye hear.” That prophet is Christ.

“This is he, that was in the church in the wilderness with the angel which spake to him in the mount Sina, and with our fathers: who received the lively oracles to give unto us”. The angel which spake to Moses in the mount Sina, at the bush and in the church in the wilderness, is the same angel by whose hand Moses was sent as a ruler and a deliverer. Moses received the lively oracles from that angel: the angel in the burning bush was Christ.

precepts.text: Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds; he had no speech impediment.
precepts.point: The LORD answered, Who hath made man's mouth? Now therefore go, and I will be with thy mouth, and teach thee what thou shalt say.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

precepts.why:
“And Moses was learned in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and was mighty in words and in deeds.” Mighty in words: Moses had no speech impediment.

He did not stutter, as is commonly taught. When he said, “I am not eloquent”, “but I am slow of speech, and of a slow tongue”, he was not fluent in the Hebrew tongue. He grew up in Pharaoh's house speaking the Egyptian language, and then spent forty years in Midian, and a language moves on in forty years.

precepts.text: Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.
precepts.point: How did we repay all that kindness? But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit: therefore he was turned to be their enemy, and he fought against them. The Most High had no choice but to turn against us, because we repaid him with rebellion.

note.label: Deuteronomy 32: The Song of Moses, Prophecy of Israel's Fall and the Most High's Vengeance

precepts.why:
“Do ye thus requite the Lord, O foolish people and unwise?” Stephen answers for every generation of Israel: “Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.” The fathers rebelled and vexed his holy Spirit, and their children always resist the Holy Ghost, the same way.

That is how the people the Most High bought, made and established requited him: rebellion in every generation, until he was turned to be their enemy.

precepts.text: Israel was still carrying the star of Remphan in the time of the apostles, the same idol.
precepts.point: Solomon built high places for Chemosh the abomination of Moab and for Molech the abomination of Ammon, and did likewise for all his strange wives who burnt incense and sacrificed to their gods. The six-pointed star called the star of David is in truth the star of Molech, an idol, and has nothing to do with righteousness.

note.label: 1 Kings 11: Solomon's Strange Wives and the Kingdom Torn

precepts.why:
“Yea, ye took up the tabernacle of Moloch, and the star of your god Remphan, figures which ye made to worship them: and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.”

Israel was still carrying the star of Remphan in the time of the apostles. It is the same idol, the star of Molech that Solomon built a high place for, “figures which ye made to worship them”. What Solomon brought in for his strange wives, Israel carried on for generations, and the Most High answered it with captivity.

precepts.text: Stephen charges the fathers as stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, always resisting the Holy Ghost, the same rebellion the Levites confess here.
precepts.point: When they cried in their trouble He heard them from heaven and delivered them many times according to His mercies, yet He did not utterly consume them, for He is a gracious and merciful God. This same stiff-necked resisting is what Stephen charged the fathers with in Acts.

note.label: Nehemiah 9: The Levites Recount the Mercy of the Most High

precepts.why:
The Levites confess what Israel did after the Most High gave them kingdoms, multiplied their children, and brought them into the land: “they were disobedient, and rebelled against thee, and cast thy law behind their backs, and slew thy prophets which testified against them to turn them to thee.” Many times He delivered them when they cried, and many times they “did evil again”, dealt proudly, “withdrew the shoulder, and hardened their neck, and would not hear.”

Stephen charged the fathers with the same thing: “Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.” The hardened neck the Levites confess is the stiff neck Stephen names, and the prophets slain in Nehemiah 9 are the prophets whose testimony the fathers resisted.

It is the same stiff-necked resisting from generation to generation: the Most High testified against them by His spirit in His prophets, and they would not give ear. Yet for His great mercies' sake He did not utterly consume them nor forsake them, “for thou art a gracious and merciful God.”

precepts.text: Ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
The Holy Ghost that Christ baptizes with is bound to the law. Stephen told the council, “Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.”

Their fathers resisted the Holy Ghost, and they did the same. To understand what the baptism of the Holy Ghost is, we have to see what resisting the Holy Ghost is, and Stephen tells it in the verses that follow.

precepts.text: What the fathers resisted was the law, received by the disposition of angels and not kept.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments, and the Comforter brings the words of Christ to remembrance.

note.label: Matthew 3: John the Baptist and the Baptism of the Holy Ghost and Fire

precepts.why:
Stephen says what the fathers resisted: “Who have received the law by the disposition of angels, and have not kept it.” They received the law by the disposition of angels and did not keep it. That is resisting the Holy Ghost.

So the Holy Ghost is bound to the law. To resist the Holy Ghost is to resist the commandments. The baptism of the Holy Ghost that Christ gives, mightier than John's water, is not apart from the law but joined to it.

precepts.text: Howbeit the most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands.
precepts.point: The saying was kept and used against him later by false witnesses at his trial.

note.label: John 2: The First Miracle and the Cleansing of the Temple

precepts.why:
“But he spake of the temple of his body.” It went over their heads, and they answered with the “Forty and six years” the temple was in building. But Stephen says, “Howbeit the most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands; as saith the prophet”.

The Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands. So the temple Christ spoke of was not the building of stone that took forty and six years. It was his body.

precepts.text: The stiffnecked resist the Holy Ghost; the first form of the Holy Ghost is the law, which they received and did not keep.
precepts.point: The Holy Ghost comes in an order that begins with the law: turn at his reproof and keep the commandments, and then he pours out his spirit and opens the understanding. Only the Most High can give the wisdom to interpret this book, which is the most purchased yet least understood book on the earth.

note.label: Acts 1: The Promise of the Father and the Kingdom Restored to Israel

precepts.why:
“Ye stiffnecked and uncircumcised in heart and ears, ye do always resist the Holy Ghost: as your fathers did, so do ye.”

The first form of the Holy Ghost is the law. Israel received it and did not keep it, and that is resisting the Holy Ghost. The order is the same as in Proverbs: turn at his reproof and keep the commandments, and then he pours out his spirit. The stiffnecked never get past the first step, as their fathers did before them.

precepts.text: The Most High told Abraham beforehand that his seed would be a stranger in a land not theirs, serve them, and be afflicted four hundred years, and that he would judge that nation; this is the prophecy Stephen is quoting.
precepts.point: Then he gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and so Abraham begat Isaac and circumcised him the eighth day, and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

precepts.why:
Stephen is quoting the prophecy the Most High gave Abraham. “Know of a surety that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them; and they shall afflict them four hundred years”. That is the strange land, the bondage and the four hundred years of being treated evil that Stephen rehearses.
